notes: cache_write is the 5-minute-TTL rate (1.25x input), cache_write_1h the 1-hour-TTL rate (2x input). Both are real: the flat JSONL field cache_creation_input_tokens hides the split, but usage.cache_creation carries it per TTL (docs/jsonl-format.md §6 shows ephemeral_1h_input_tokens=6935 / ephemeral_5m_input_tokens=0 on a real Claude Code turn) — 1h is NOT rare, and pricing it at the 5m rate under-bills by 37.5%. Ingest stores the split in turns.cache_write_5m_tokens / cache_write_1h_tokens (migration 0075); a turn with no cache_creation object (older transcripts) attributes the whole total to 5m, so its cost is unchanged.

usage.speed ("standard" / "fast") selects the SKU: a fast turn bills at the sibling <model>-fast row, resolved by cost.PriceForSpeed AFTER the model id resolves to its pricing key — appending -fast to a date-suffixed id would fall back onto standard rates and look like a hit. Stored in turns.speed (migration 0075).
claude-sonnet-5 uses introductory pricing valid through 2026-08-31 ($3 in / $15 out after) — update this file and run `swarmery recost` on 2026-09-01.

claude-opus-5-5 rates confirmed against the official Anthropic pricing page (2026-09-22): $4 in / $20 out / $0.20 cache-read / $5 cache-write-5m / $8 cache-write-1h. Two things differ from the rest of the Opus tier: it is CHEAPER than Opus 5 ($5/$25), and its cache-read multiplier is 0.05x base input, not the usual 0.1x — do not derive cache_read by multiplying input by 0.1 here.

claude-opus-5-5 vs claude-opus-5 is a longest-prefix HAZARD, not just two rows: the id claude-opus-5-5[1m] is not matched by the claude-opus-5-5- prefix (bracket, not dash) but IS matched by claude-opus-5-, which would bill it at Opus 5 rates. cost.PriceFor strips a trailing [..] context-window marker before lookup so that cannot happen; TestOpus55NotMispricedAsOpus5 pins it. Any future model whose id extends an existing key inherits the same hazard.

claude-opus-5 rates confirmed against the official Anthropic pricing page (2026-07-25): $5 in / $25 out / $0.50 cache-read / $6.25 cache-write-5m — identical to the Opus 4.5-4.8 tier. Full 1M context window is standard-priced with NO long-context multiplier (a 900k-token request is billed per-token like a 9k one).

claude-opus-5-fast is a SEPARATE SKU at 2x standard ($10 in / $50 out) and does NOT combine with the Batch API — priced explicitly so a speed:"fast" session is not silently mapped to standard pricing by the claude-opus-5- prefix fallback (longest-prefix match picks claude-opus-5-fast- first).

Tokenizer change (models >= 4.7, incl. Opus 5): the newer tokenizer emits ~30% more tokens for the same text. Per-token rates are unchanged, but token COUNTS rise — the main recost risk when comparing Opus 5 sessions against Opus 4.5/4.6 or Sonnet 4.6 history.
Cache reads bill at 0.1x base input ($0.50/MTok). Long repo-context agent sessions land most input here — track cache_read separately from base input when reasoning about cost.
claude-opus-4-8 (and 4-7/4-6/4-5) retained to price backfilled historical transcripts from before the Opus 5 cutover.
claude-opus-4-1 is deprecated (retires 2026-08-05); kept to price backfilled historical transcripts.

Keys in `models` match model ids exactly as they appear in JSONL assistant records (docs/jsonl-format.md §6). `fallback_prefixes` maps date-suffixed ids (e.g. claude-haiku-4-5-20251001) to a pricing key via longest-prefix match.
